newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices flat, spot LSWR firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices flat, spot LSWR firmer.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were largely unchanged in late afternoon trade on Wednesday amid a lack of fresh incentives, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half February was bid at $232.00, while offers were notionally assessed at around $234.00.
Second-half February was quoted at $229.00/231.00, little changed from late Tuesday levels.
Backwardation remained steep in inter-month naphtha spreads, with first-half February/first-half March discussed at plus $5.50/6.50, compared with Tuesday's plus $5.50/6.00.
In physical naphtha trading, a major refiner said it bought a spot cargo for first-half January delivery. The price was rumoured to be around $10.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes.

A Japanese trading house was said to have bought 200,000 barrels of Indonesian low-sulphur waxy residue cargoes from a Western major at around 90 cents over the Pertamina formula for end-December loading.
Levels for Indonesian cargoes were mainly assessed at the formula plus 60 to 70 cents late last month.
The trader was believed to co-load the Indonesian lots with Malaysian term cargoes. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
